spec_fidelity: The HUD and drifting creatures are present, but the requested player with a net is absent and the required Collection button is replaced by an ambiguous NEW COLLECTION pill. The play field therefore does not visibly read as a creature-catching interaction.
unity: The black field, restrained cyan/magenta bioluminescence, thin grid, and compact HUD share a coherent nocturnal sci-fi language, but the isolated center pill feels disconnected from both the HUD and the play action.
variety: All creatures use nearly the same glowing capsule silhouette and size, producing repetition rather than a living scene; depth, species identity, and a clear player-versus-target focal relationship are missing.
conflict: Unity benefits from the narrow neon grammar, while Variety calls for distinct creatures; Fidelity demands adding the player and Collection action without turning the sparse field into a cluttered dashboard.
resolution: Retain the two-accent bioluminescent world and shared glow treatment, but vary creature silhouettes, scale, and motion trails by species and introduce one grounded player/net focal element plus a clearly labeled Collection control.
moderator_revision: Make the catching interaction unmistakable: add a visible player silhouette near the lower field holding a readable net aimed toward a nearby creature, and replace NEW COLLECTION with a clearly labeled COLLECTION button integrated beside the captured-count HUD or lower control rail. Keep the black/cyan/magenta bioluminescent system, but redesign the creatures into 3–4 related species silhouettes with meaningful size, fin/wing/tail, depth, and glow-intensity variation. Use the same soft organic geometry and restrained palette across all species, strengthen the play-field boundary and depth grid, and arrange the player plus nearest target as the main focal encounter without filling every empty area.
